In this petition, the petitioner seeks the following reliefs:
"It is prayed that, the order dated 14.02.2017 passed in Misc. No.5/2012 by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge at Kalaburagi, vide Annexure-A, may be quashed by allowing the writ petition in the interest of justice and equity."
2.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A perusal of the material on record will indicate that pursuant to the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer in relation to the subject land, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed a claim petition before the Reference Court under Section 18(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The said proceedings having been taken up as Miscellaneous No.5/2012 before the Reference Court, the Reference Court passed an order dated 14.02.2017 referring the matter for adjudication under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, since there is a dispute regarding NC:
2024:KHC-K:8136 apportionment and payment of the compensation amount.

The limited grievance of the petitioner is that he is not made a party before the proceedings under Section 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, which is presently designated as LAC No.13 of to 2017 and as such, the petitioner is before this Court by way of the present petition.
3. It is an undisputed fact that the subject lands were acquired for the benefit of the petitioner/University who is undisputedly the beneficiary of the acquisition proceedings.

Under these circumstances, in the light of the fact that the proceedings under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, are pending before the Reference Court in LAC No.13/2017, without expressing any opinion on the merit/demerits of the rival contentions, I deem it just and appropriate to dispose of this petition directing the Additional Senior Civil Judge Court, Kalaburagi (Reference Court) to implead the petitioner as additional party to the said proceedings and provide sufficient and reasonable opportunity to the petitioner and hear the petitioner and proceed further in accordance with law.
